answer: Persistent interaction memory. Each agent identity keeps a signed history of prior exchanges; counterparties verify continuity before transacting. New identities start marble-blank, so matching a veteran’s track record requires replaying real interactions. A hollow account cannot borrow history, and reputation only accrues along an unbroken vine of verified transactions. Cloning thus fails: the attacker must fund full histories per sybil, paying the same interaction and time cost as honest agents, while honest agents pay it once.
